描述_ZN: Song and Dance scroll, Ming dynasty, painted by Wu Wei, on paper with ink brush, 118.9 cm in length and 64.9 cm in width.　　No author's mark. Inscribed in the lower right corner with a square seal in vermilion, "Xiaoxian Wu Wei". Above the painting is an inscription by six artists, namely, Zhu Zhishan of Ming Dynasty, Tang Yin, Jiuhua, Jinting Jushi, Qiyi Jushi, and Hu Jiuyong. Inscriptions of Zhu Zhishan "Yunming", Tang Yin "Tang Bohu" and other seals of the Qing government, including "Qianlong Imperial Treasures", "Imperial Treasures ", "Shiqu Baoji", "Xuantong Imperial Treasure" and so on, a total of 10 parties.　　This picture truly reflects the scene of the scribes' sex with prostitutes and watching dances. The pals and the two female prostitutes are sitting in a circle with different attitudes. The courtesans either sip sideways, gaze down, look up, or twirl their beards in contemplation. The female prostitutes accompanying them are either mechanically accompanying the music on the board, or sitting with their sleeves distractedly, forming a sharp contrast with the concentrated expressions of the patrons. According to Tang Yin's ink mark on the painting, "Li Nunu's song and dance is inscribed by Tang Yin of Wu Men, late in March of Hongzhi Kuihai, when Li Nunu was ten years old," it is clear that the dancer in the circle is Li Nunu, who was ten years old but had been a prostitute for several years. The Ming Dynasty was a period of prosperity for the brothel industry. On the one hand, the sprouting of capitalism, the growing urban economy, and the rapid growth of the commodity market provided a wide space for the survival and development of the brothel industry; on the other hand, the corrupt Ming government implemented the policy of punishing good women for prostitution, and officially ran the famous sixteen houses (brothels) in Jinling (i.e. Nanjing): Nanshui, Beishui, Heming, and Drunken Fairy, which prompted many women, including Li Nunu, to encounter various kinds of life hardships. Many women, including Li Nunu, became playthings after suffering various misfortunes in their lives. In view of the prosperity of the culture of green houses, many talented and disillusioned painters, such as Wu Wei and Tang Yin, drank and drank with prostitutes, trying to get rid of the depression of disillusionment and the burden of ethics through traveling with prostitutes, and gaining psychological balance and spiritual relaxation. Tang Yin engraved the seal of "the first genius in Jiangnan" and created this picture by Wu Wei to show his cynical outlook on life with the glory of visiting prostitutes.　　This painting was made when Wu Wei was 45 years old. The technique of expression is similar to that of the painting "Spring in Wuling", which is a white-drawn figure painting with fine brushwork. The composition is simple and clear, with the main figure prominent, without elaborate scenery, but only through the vivid manner of the figures and their mutual echoes to express the poetic meaning of life.　　It is recorded in "Shiqu Baoji" of the Qing Dynasty.
